name: Rest & Recovery
content:
RESTING DURING A QUEST

During the Quest phase of play, party members may take one Short Rest and one Long Rest per day. The Quests' Keeping may alter the effects of resting (see the Treasure, Keeping & Equipment section), but these are the default effects:

SHORT REST

At least 1 hour of undisturbed rest is considered a SHORT REST. If you are not Helpless, you recover Endurance equal to your BODY score.

LONG REST

At least 6 consecutive hours of undisturbed rest is considered a LONG REST:

  • You recover all of your Endurance, minus your current Injury score. If you’re Helpless, you instead recover Endurance equal to your BODY score (do not subtract your Injury score).

  • If you have 0 Hope, you regain 1 Hope.

If a Long Rest is interrupted by one hour or more of activity or any amount of combat, you instead gain the benefits of a Short Rest.

INTERMEZZO

An Intermezzo (see Phases of Play) is another opportunity to rest and recover from the hardships of the Questing life. In addition to the broad narrative possibilities of an Intermezzo, there are some specific actions characters may choose to take to restore their strength:

DISTRIBUTE COMPAGNIA

Any Compagnia (see Quest Mechanics) left over at the end of a Quest may be distributed among those who participated in the Quest. Each point distributed in this way removes 1 Shadow or clears 1 Condition for the recipient. Players should reach consensus about how to distribute the points before doing so.

TREAT INJURIES

For each day spent in the care of a skilled healer, remove 1 Injury. Depending on the circumstances, the GM may require that you maintain a certain Keeping or spend an amount of Treasure to account for the healer’s wages (see Treasure & Keeping).

If a player character is acting as the skilled healer, for each day where they are doing so, they must roll Aid against the current Injury of the character they are trying to heal. On a pass, remove Injury equal to the difference between the Aid check result and the current Injury. No effect on a failure.

For example, if the healing character rolls 13 on an Aid check and the injured character has 10 Injury, they remove 3 Injury for that day.

STRENGTHEN COMPAGNIA

If you and another player character spend the entire Intermezzo in one another's company, choose two effects:

  • You each gain 1 Hope.

  • You each remove 1 Shadow.

  • You each clear one Condition.

  • If both of you participate in the next Quest, the party starts the Quest with 1 additional Compagnia.

Describe how you spend your time together and how it strengthens your bond.

CLEAR CONDITIONS

The narrative requirements for clearing Conditions during an Intermezzo are the same as during a Quest, but in some situations it may be wise to deal with those emotions in a more controlled environment than during a Quest. See Conditions.
